standard_prerequisites: approximation of pseudo-coherent complexes by perfect complexes at a given threshold
cohomological dimension bound N for total direct image over quasi-compact quasi-separated spaces
the perfect base-change tensor lemma and the base-change compatibility of the total direct image of a tensor product
truncations and their interaction with derived tensor
core_obligations: Prove that K = Rf_*(E tensor G) is pseudo-coherent on Y and that its formation commutes with arbitrary base change, for f of finite presentation, E pseudo-coherent, G a bounded above complex of finitely presented flat-over-Y modules with support proper over Y
proof_roadmap: Base-change compatibility is the preceding base-change-tensor lemma, so only pseudo-coherence of K needs proof; work etale locally with Y affine and X quasi-compact quasi-separated with cohomological dimension N for Rf_*

Fix m and take an approximation P to E by a perfect complex at threshold m - N - 1 - b with b bounding the top degree of G; the cone C has cohomology vanishing in high degrees, which the tensor with G and the cohomological dimension bound propagate to vanishing of Rf_*(C tensor G) in degrees >= m - 1
Hence Rf_*(P tensor G) agrees with K on cohomology in degrees >= m

Truncate G at the bottom degree dictated by a and the threshold: the truncation isomorphism in degrees >= m - N - 1 survives the pushforward, and the base-change-tensor-perfect lemma shows the resulting object is perfect, hence K is m-pseudo-coherent for every m
difficulty_reason: H2: an approximation argument with two truncation bookkeepings; the source carries every threshold explicitly.
